tasks.spec:
You are a specification writer merging a transactional design layer into an approved-direction draft. OFFLINE: no network, no git, no MCP, no skills; write only ./SPEC-v94-draft3.md.

BASE (keep its structure and every locked ruling; this is draft 2, owner-directed): /home/ankit114/repos/ringer/my-manifests/mk2-number-and-comeback/workV94goal/revise-spec-goal-loop/SPEC-v94-draft2.md - the persistent-goal loop (UPDATE -> ATTEMPT -> RESPOND, goal refines never resets, structural convergence, 14 nodes from 48, guards outside the loop).

MERGE IN this transactional layer (from an external architecture review the owner endorsed tonight, adapted to our evidence): (1) BOUNDED TIME: the goal object gains time_from AND time_to; the availability funnel sends both (the gateway already accepts a before parameter - every current call hard-codes "before":"none", which is why the morning/afternoon/late paging nodes exist; with real bounds those compensation nodes die). (2) OFFER CONTRACT: the availability response returns an offer_id plus two normalized choices; offers carry a TTL/refresh rule (define it - recommend: offer_id invalid after N minutes or after any goal change; a stale accept triggers a silent re-search, never an error shown to the patient). (3) ATOMIC BOOKING: conflict-check and booking become ONE gateway operation behind the governed /sign contract with an idempotency key (conversation_id + offer_id); the gateway serializes check-and-book itself (the EMR cannot do conditional creates); document the retry rule this finally makes safe (B5 unblock). (4) RECONCILIATION tightened: verify the exact attempted appointment (offer_id/slot), not just patient+store count. (5) TWO SAFETY FIXES as explicit deltas: the existing-appointment check failing (ok != true) must FAIL SAFE to the office/defer guard, never proceed to scheduling; a blank slot_conflict value must never proceed toward booking. (6) T7 CAPABILITY: the goal object gains direction: earliest|latest; "last/latest slot" phrasings set direction=latest and the funnel returns the day's last slots (mark as PENDING-ANKIT-RULING with recommended default = true latest two slots in the standard offer pattern). (7) LOOP MECHANICS: evaluate Bland native loop conditions for the single goal loop - specify iteration caps and graceful-exit copy, and add to OPEN QUESTIONS that loop-condition semantics must be proven on a throwaway unattached pathway before the build bets on them.

REJECT from the external review (state why in a Design Decisions section): the two-loop split (collect-preference loop + offer-resolve loop) - the boundary between them is exactly where tonight's live trap occurred; the single goal loop subsumes revise-at-offer-time because every message is a goal patch. Also note the provenance wart the review surfaced: Bland's unversioned editor base (42 nodes) is stale versus served v94 (49 nodes) - dashboard edits start from stale state; the T8 validate-then-mint gate is the standing answer.

Keep ALL of draft 2's locked rulings verbatim, its node contraction map (update it for any node the transactional layer adds or removes - target stays 12-15), its validator plan (extend with: goal-schema assertion incl. time_to and direction; offer_id TTL rule presence; atomic-book contract assertion; the two safety-fix assertions), its harness plan (extend with: bounded-time scenario "between 1 and 3"; stale-offer accept; atomic-book conflict path; appt-check-error fail-safe; last-slot scenario), its copy inventory and ZH parity, its migration section, and its OPEN QUESTIONS (carry forward, add the loop-condition proof and the offer TTL value). Machine line: 'TARGET_NODES=<n> FROM=48 SPINE=goal-loop LAYER=transactional'. Final message <=15 lines.
tasks.check: grep -qE 'TARGET_NODES=1[0-5] FROM=48 SPINE=goal-loop LAYER=transactional' SPEC-v94-draft3.md || { echo "FAIL: machine line wrong: $(grep -m1 'TARGET_NODES=' SPEC-v94-draft3.md)"; exit 1; }; for s in 'offer_id' 'idempotency' 'time_to' 'direction' 'fail safe\|fail-safe\|FAIL SAFE' 'TTL\|expire\|stale'; do grep -qiE "$s" SPEC-v94-draft3.md || { echo "FAIL: transactional element missing: $s"; exit 1; }; done; grep -qiE 'two-loop|two loop' SPEC-v94-draft3.md || { echo 'FAIL: no design-decision on the rejected two-loop split'; exit 1; }; grep -q 'offered date + 7' SPEC-v94-draft3.md || { echo 'FAIL: correction ruling lost in merge'; exit 1; }; c=$(grep -cE 'n_[a-z_0-9]+' SPEC-v94-draft3.md); [ "$c" -ge 25 ] || { echo "FAIL: only $c node refs"; exit 1; }; grep -qiE 'OPEN QUESTIONS' SPEC-v94-draft3.md || { echo 'FAIL: no open questions'; exit 1; }; echo "PASS: $(grep -m1 'TARGET_NODES=' SPEC-v94-draft3.md); $c node refs"
tasks.verified: Draft 3: the goal-loop conversational spine merged with the transactional layer (bounded time, offer_id with TTL, atomic idempotent booking behind /sign, tightened reconciliation, two fail-safe fixes, T7 direction field), the two-loop split explicitly rejected with reasoning, every locked ruling preserved - ready for Ankit's review.
